text: 64 teams in a knockout cup: five rounds and a final. Rounds 1 and 2: two pots, one with the Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs and one with the amateur teams; a ball is drawn from the amateur pot first, then from the other, and the team drawn first is always at home, so in these rounds an amateur team drawn against a licensed club is at home because of the draw order, not by a separate rule. From the round of 16: one pot, the team drawn first is at home, but between a licensed team and an amateur team the amateur team is at home, as an explicit rule. Level after normal time: extra time of 2 x 15 minutes, then penalties. The final is played at the venue the DFB GmbH & Co. KG fixes.

text: Entry rules: 64 teams. The Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs of the season just ended, the cup winners of the 21 regional associations, and the champion and the next three of the 3. Liga of the season just ended. The remaining places up to 64 go to the associations with the most men's teams, at most one extra each, decided by the DFB's Fachgruppe Spielbetriebe from the current membership statistics; every association must send at least one amateur team. Second teams of licensed clubs may not enter (since 2008-09), no club may enter two teams (since 2009-10), and the club's status in the season being played counts. A regional cup winner that is a second team or already qualified is replaced by the next eligible team of that cup; a 3. Liga qualifier that is a second team or already qualified through its regional cup is replaced by the next eligible 3. Liga team or the next eligible team of that cup. Merged teams (Spielgemeinschaften) may not enter. Each entrant must declare an advertising-free stadium for a live TV match, which need not be in its own town.

text: Draw and home right. Rounds 1 and 2: two pots, one with the Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga clubs and one with the amateur teams, by status in the season being played; in round 1 the clubs promoted to the 2. Bundesliga and the previous season's 15th of the 2. Bundesliga (and its 16th if it stayed up through the play-off) go in the amateur pot. Home right cannot be given up; two teams that named the same stadium and are drawn together is not a waiver. Final at the venue the DFB GmbH & Co. KG fixes. text: Final table in 2026-27, as the FIGC's Federal Council decided on 26 May 2026 on the proposal of the Lega Calcio Serie A, departing for this season from art. 51 of the NOIF. If two teams finish level on points in first place, the title (Campione d'Italia) goes to the winner of a single play-off match at the home of the team better placed in the mini-table (classifica avulsa); if it is level after normal time, there is no extra time and penalties decide. Where more than two teams are level, and for all the other places in the table, the classifica avulsa decides in this order: a) points in the matches between the teams concerned, b) goal difference in those matches, c) goal difference over the whole championship, d) goals scored over the whole championship, e) drawing of lots. If a team that would play the play-off is a finalist in a UEFA competition, the classifica avulsa decides instead. The number of clubs, matches per club and points per win are not stated on any page of the organiser or the federation that could be read (see the Wikipedia row).
basis: published: FIGC Comunicato Ufficiale n. 244/A for the season 2026/2027, read in full

text: According to the FIGC's communiqué for 2026-27: if the teams in 17th and 18th place finish level on points, a two-legged play-off (spareggio) decides which stays in Serie A. If more than two teams are level, the classifica avulsa picks the two; if one of them is a finalist in a UEFA competition, the classifica avulsa decides instead. How many clubs go down and how many come up from Serie B is not stated on a page of the organiser or the federation that could be read (see the Wikipedia row).
